title: Zero-wise independence fools circuits
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\varepsilon>1$, and let $S$ be any set of Boolean circuits on $n$ inputs. Every probability distribution on Boolean inputs that is independent on every set of at most zero coordinates fools $S$ with error at most $\varepsilon$: for every such distribution $\mu$ and every $C\in S$, the absolute difference between the acceptance probabilities of $C$ under $\mu$ and under the uniform distribution is at most $\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ is a set of circuits on $n$ Boolean inputs
